sheets.light: Bright, indirect light. A metre back from an east or south window is ideal.
sheets.water: Water when the top 5 cm of soil is dry, roughly every 8 to 10 days in summer and every 14 days in winter.
sheets.notes: Wipe leaves monthly. Yellow lower leaves usually mean overwatering. Mildly toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

sheets.light: Tolerates low light, happiest in medium indirect light.
sheets.water: Water every 3 to 4 weeks. Let the pot dry out completely between waterings.
sheets.notes: Rot from soggy soil is the main killer. Repot only when roots crack the pot.

sheets.light: Low to bright indirect light. Variegation fades in deep shade.
sheets.water: Water when the top 3 cm of soil is dry, about every 7 to 10 days. Leaves droop when thirsty and recover within hours.
sheets.notes: Easy to propagate in water from a node cutting. Mildly toxic to pets.

sheets.light: Bright, indirect light, and it hates being moved. Rotate a quarter turn each month.
sheets.water: Water when the top 5 cm of soil is dry, about every 7 days. Never let it sit in a saucer of water.
sheets.notes: Brown spots on the edges mean uneven watering or a draught. Dust the leaves every few weeks.

sheets.water: Water every 3 weeks. Stores water in its rhizomes, so it forgives missed waterings.
sheets.notes: Slow grower. Wrinkled stems mean it is underwatered. Toxic if eaten, wash hands after pruning.

sheets.light: Medium to low indirect light. Direct sun scorches the leaves.
sheets.water: Keep soil lightly moist, about every 5 to 7 days. Droops dramatically when thirsty.
sheets.notes: Brown leaf tips mean dry air or tap water with a lot of minerals. Toxic to cats and dogs.
